newsitem.title: BRAZIL: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN WINS SEVENTH RACE IN A ROW.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN WINS SEVENTH RACE IN A ROW.

text.p: Michael Doohan won his seventh consecutive race to move closer to the 500cc world motorcycling title at the Brazilian Grand Prix on Sunday.
The Australian, aiming to take his fourth world championship in a row, increased his apparently invincible championship lead after leading from the first lap.

Doohan fought off a stiff challenge from Japan's Tadayuki Okada, who was on his tail for the whole race, after the two Honda team mates sped clear of the field early in the race. Italian Luca Cadalora was third on a Yamaha.
Okada made several attempts to pass but was foiled each time by the Australian, who has won nine out of 10 races this season.

Spain's Carlos Checa, who briefly led for the first half of the first lap, crashed out in spectacular style in the second lap after clipping the back wheel of Japan's Norick Abe but walked away apparently unscathed.
Okada's second place moved him into second place in the championship, ahead of compatriot Nobuatsu Aoki, who finished fourth.
Doohan could have won the title here if Okada and Aoki had finished lower down the field, but the result means the championship race is still open, although only in theory.
